evidence.title: Nonlinear modeling and torsional vibration analysis of heavy-duty vehicle powertrain system during acceleration
evidence.abstract: The vehicle acceleration process is often accompanied by torsional vibration of the powertrain system. Poor torsional vibration performance significantly influences the driving comfort of the vehicle and the reliability of powertrain components. Compared to passenger cars, commercial vehicles, especially the heavy-duty truck, exhibit more complicated vibration behaviors during acceleration due to the multiple power branches, various gears, and different working conditions. This article presents systematic research on the modeling method, vibration characteristics, mechanism, and influence factors of the torsional resonance of the heavy-duty vehicle during acceleration. A 16-DOF powertrain model considering multiple nonlinearities of the system is proposed and experimentally validated reliable. Numerical and experimental studies are carried out to investigate the vibration characteristics and mechanism of the heavy-duty vehicle powertrain, and the modal energies and parameter influences are also discussed. Besides, an optimization example is presented to analyze the potential vibration attenuation performance of optimizing the clutch parameters. The results indicate that the overall powertrain mode of the heavy-duty vehicle tends to be aroused by the engine firing frequency during accelerating, inducing violent speed fluctuations of the powertrain components between the clutch and half-shafts. The clutch parameters have significant impacts on the powertrain resonance, and the vibration amplitude of the powertrain system can be effectively attenuated to acceptable levels by optimally designing the clutch parameters

A classical control approach to the power management of an all-electric hybrid

evidence.abstract:
Modern hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) often employ all-electric powertrains
that utilise hybrid sources of power and energy; such as batteries, fuel cells
and ultracapacitors. This paper describes the design, simulation and
experimental verification of a power management control system that manages a
high voltage battery, a DC-DC boost converter and an ultracapacitor within a
front-wheel drive HEV in which the motive power for the vehicle comes from two
electrical machines. As part of this study, consideration is given to the
complete control system design life-cycle including plant model development,
algorithm design and software implementation on the target electronic control
unit (ECU). Off-line simulation and initial experimental results are presented
showing the vehicle operating on a powertrain dynamometer as one means of
demonstrating the ability of the ultracapacitor to limit the transient demands
placed on the battery during periods of vehicle acceleration and regenerative
braking

evidence.title: Torsional vibration analysis of automotive drivelines
evidence.abstract:
One of the most important source of noise and vibrations associated with vehicles is the vibration of driveline systems. Such phenomena are subjectively associated with

customer complaints. In this study the torsional vibrations of driveline systems were investigated using discretised and lumped mass models of the system.



In the literature, many of the problems associated with torsional vibrations and refinement in drivelines have been tackled through relatively simple, lumped mass models combinedw ith experimentalm easurements. However, some problems remain particularly where instabilities occur or complex coupling with other vehicle vibration modes exists. The review of previous work showed that although it is important to understand the dynamic behaviour of the individual driveline components; for example, engine, clutch, gearbox, etc., the whole system must be analysed together because of all the coupling which occurs.



The main source of excitation for torsional vibration of the driveline system is the engine fluctuating torque. A computer program using MATLAB subroutines was developed to obtain this fluctuation torque for different engine parameters for subsequent use in the modelling.



A substructure approach, using stiffness coupling technique with combined use of residual flexibility and modal synthesis, was used to analyse free and forced vibrations

of the system, as a linear system. A computer program using MATLAB subroutines was designed to facilitate application of this technique. Good agreement between results for the overall system model and substructure model was found even for a few considered modes. This substructure technique offers significant computational advantages over other methods.

torsional vibrations was investigated. The effect of backlash in the driveline system was significant and, as expected, vibration levels increased as backlash increased.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. custody_records.raw_content: The vehicle acceleration process is often accompanied by torsional vibration of the powertrain system. Poor torsional vibration performance significantly influences the driving comfort of the vehicle and the reliability of powertrain components. Compared to passenger cars, commercial vehicles, especially the heavy-duty truck, exhibit more complicated vibration behaviors during acceleration due to the multiple power branches, various gears, and different working conditions. This article presents systematic research on the modeling method, vibration characteristics, mechanism, and influence factors of the torsional resonance of the heavy-duty vehicle during acceleration. A 16-DOF powertrain model considering multiple nonlinearities of the system is proposed and experimentally validated reliable. Numerical and experimental studies are carried out to investigate the vibration characteristics and mechanism of the heavy-duty vehicle powertrain, and the modal energies and parameter influences are also discussed. Besides, an optimization example is presented to analyze the potential vibration attenuation performance of optimizing the clutch parameters. The results indicate that the overall powertrain mode of the heavy-duty vehicle tends to be aroused by the engine firing frequency during accelerating, inducing violent speed fluctuations of the powertrain components between the clutch and half-shafts. The clutch parameters have significant impacts on the powertrain resonance, and the vibration amplitude of the powertrain system can be effectively attenuated to acceptable levels by optimally designing the clutch parameters

Modern hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) often employ all-electric powertrains
that utilise hybrid sources of power and energy; such as batteries, fuel cells
and ultracapacitors. This paper describes the design, simulation and
experimental verification of a power management control system that manages a
high voltage battery, a DC-DC boost converter and an ultracapacitor within a
front-wheel drive HEV in which the motive power for the vehicle comes from two
electrical machines. As part of this study, consideration is given to the
complete control system design life-cycle including plant model development,
algorithm design and software implementation on the target electronic control
unit (ECU). Off-line simulation and initial experimental results are presented
showing the vehicle operating on a powertrain dynamometer as one means of
demonstrating the ability of the ultracapacitor to limit the transient demands
placed on the battery during periods of vehicle acceleration and regenerative
braking

One of the most important source of noise and vibrations associated with vehicles is the vibration of driveline systems. Such phenomena are subjectively associated with

customer complaints. In this study the torsional vibrations of driveline systems were investigated using discretised and lumped mass models of the system.



In the literature, many of the problems associated with torsional vibrations and refinement in drivelines have been tackled through relatively simple, lumped mass models combinedw ith experimentalm easurements. However, some problems remain particularly where instabilities occur or complex coupling with other vehicle vibration modes exists. The review of previous work showed that although it is important to understand the dynamic behaviour of the individual driveline components; for example, engine, clutch, gearbox, etc., the whole system must be analysed together because of all the coupling which occurs.



The main source of excitation for torsional vibration of the driveline system is the engine fluctuating torque. A computer program using MATLAB subroutines was developed to obtain this fluctuation torque for different engine parameters for subsequent use in the modelling.



A substructure approach, using stiffness coupling technique with combined use of residual flexibility and modal synthesis, was used to analyse free and forced vibrations

of the system, as a linear system. A computer program using MATLAB subroutines was designed to facilitate application of this technique. Good agreement between results for the overall system model and substructure model was found even for a few considered modes. This substructure technique offers significant computational advantages over other methods.
